translation:
It was necessary for Prahlad to say this — he could not tell the true fact, that he had cleverly escaped from the funeral pyre and so remained alive, because the cruel father would have caused further trouble. But the father accepted this account. He also expressed grief over Holika's death, shedding crocodile tears.

As if this were not enough, the world too came to accept this account. Many came to believe that Holika had received a boon — how then could she have died? She could not possibly burn! Even today this belief has taken root among us to such an extent that, considering it a miracle, many walk on the burning embers of Holi. Their claim is that all this is Holika's own glory, and many have come to regard her as a goddess — that though one walks on the Holi fire one is not burnt. But no one is willing to understand the true fact; everyone has been led along by religious superstition, everyone has become blind to this. No one wants to open their eyes and look — a herd mentality has taken hold.

It is true that walking momentarily on burning embers causes no injury. But this is because, after years of practice, the skin on the soles of the feet becomes thick and the nerve-endings of the sensory system get deadened, so that no sensation of heat is felt. But no human being can stand still on such embers for hours — this is a scientific law: fire is capable of burning anything, and its touch causes injury. But through practice and repeated effort it becomes possible to walk on it for a few moments; there is no miracle in this. But why the world, having lost its senses in religious superstition, is not willing to understand such a plain truth — that itself is the big question.

Jivanji Maharaj explained, giving a solid scientific reason, that fire burns any object that has form. Nothing escapes it — even if it be the Supreme Being (Parbrahm) come in an incarnation, or, in doubt, merely a human being, it will still burn. This is an eternal law, unalterable at any time or age. Therefore sensible people, upon reading and hearing the many mythological tales, should reflect that a scientific law never changes. If Prahlad had touched a hot, burning spot, he would surely have been burnt. Further, as we have already said, if the Supreme Being too takes incarnation in the world in doubtful bodily form, then the law that governs the world must certainly apply to him as well. Then why was Lord Narsinh not burnt? We do not wish to go into the depths of the mythological facts — Jivanji Maharaj too, having pointed to the scientific fact, has stepped aside from the matter, because engaging in debate is not the devotees' task. We only believe and know this much: that the devotee Prahlad was saved, and that divine power triumphed over demonic power. The victory of truth over untruth is our only aim.

Moreover, since devotee Prahlad was rescued and delivered from calamity, then whoever saved him is our Lord (Parmeshwar); we do not wish to enter into any debate about it — the world may consider the one who protected Prahlad to be the incarnation of Narsinh or anyone else, but for us the one formless, unmanifest Supreme Being (Niranjan Nirakar Parbrahm) alone is sufficient. We do not wish to enter into debates over incarnations, nor do we wish to worship or venerate any incarnations. Through a verse from the Niranjan Purana the form of God has been described, and, presenting an alternative view, it is said: if God has no form, then what is one to make of his manifesting from the pillar for Prahlad's sake? For this, the Haarmala (Garland) hymn has been presented. That hymn corresponds to the Bhagavat, Canto 10, Chapter 43, verse 17:

_Mallanam ashani nrinam natvarah, strinam smaro murtiman |
Gopanam svajano-satam kshitibhujam shasta svapitroh shishuh ||
Mrityur bhojapater virat cha vidusham tattvam param yoginam |
Vrishninam paradevateti vidito rangam gatah sagrajah ||3||_
(At the time when Lord Shri Krishna, together with Balram, entered the wrestling arena, he appeared to the wrestlers as one with a body hard as a thunderbolt, to ordinary men as the finest of men, to women as Kamadev — the god of love — in bodily form, to the cowherds as their own kinsman, to the wicked kings as the ruler who metes out punishment, to the elders, as venerable as their own parents, as a mere child, to Kansa as death itself, to the ignorant as the cosmic form (Virat), to the yogis as the Supreme Reality, and to the Vrishni clan, foremost among devotees, as their own chosen deity. Each experienced, according to his own disposition, the rasa — the aesthetic sentiment — of terror, wonder, romance, laughter, heroism, parental affection, fear, disgust, peace, or loving devotion.)

It is stated in Registration No. 846, page 41, that this Damodarashram was an ascetic Vedantic poet. He was a resident of Siddhpur and lived by Bindu Sarovar; he lived fifty years after Bhalan. Another view holds that he lived about five hundred to five hundred twenty-five years ago near Karnali by Chandod, and that he was a follower of the Shankar school. Ra' Mangalik, the king of Junagadh, at the instigation of these ascetic renunciants, persecuted Narsinh Mehta over the garland of Lord Damodar; because of this, Narsinh Mehta went to live with his daughter in Una, and passed away there. But the king was held at fault for wronging this devotee, and so Mahmud Begada forcibly converted this king and made him a Muslim; that king's grave was in Manek Chowk in Ahmedabad. Because Mahmud Begada conquered two forts, he came to be called "Begado" (the one of two forts); he had also conquered the second fort, Pavagadh.

_Samvat 1572 na Magsar Sud-7 Bhomvare, Shri Damodarji e apyo Mehtaji ne haar re_
(In Samvat 1572, on Tuesday, the seventh day of the bright half of Magsar, Shri Damodarji gave Mehtaji the garland) — this is one line from the Haarmala hymn. By offering this composition of Narsinh Mehta, Jivanji Maharaj sought to explain what would come of quarreling over whether God has form or is formless, and what he is truly like. God appears to each person according to that person's own disposition; God takes on the form suited to each one's taste and nature. God is the Lord of all — so how could he be said to have a fixed form? And yet he took Hiranyakashyapu onto his lap and tore him apart — so how could he be called formless either? Moreover, that which has form cannot survive fire. So, explaining and establishing the truth of form and formlessness to devotees such as Devdas, Kalyandas, Haridas, and Ramdas, Jivanji Maharaj said that the God who protected Prahlad is the very God we worship. Sakhi (couplet) —

1. When the demon Hiranyakashyapu became terrifying, God assumed the form of Narsinh and protected the devotee Prahlad, and there was rejoicing and cries of victory throughout the world over his triumph.

2. Ram is truly and verily God, and he is capable of shattering the heads of all and keeping everyone under his control; therefore worship that very God who was the protector of Prahlad.

3. Ramchandra is truly God — he who held up Mount Govardhan upon his hand, and he who went to Janakpuri, broke the bow, and married Sitaji.

_Naamroop dou Jivana, Sadguru kahe samajhai |
Prahlad kaso aparadh, je roope raha bandhai ||5||_
(Regarding both the Name and the Form of God, the true guru explains: Prahlad had to endure hardship because of one flaw in him — he was attached only to the Form of God, without having understood, through a true guru, the union of Name and Form. God takes whatever form the devotee holds in mind; but one who understands the intricacy of Name and Form attains God with ease.)

_Prahlad bichara kaha kare, kaman ki ghundi nahi |
Naame baho Jivana, chhodo Vaikunth mahi ||6||_
(What could poor Prahlad do — he was helpless. In his heart he held no knot of ill-will toward anyone, whether father or God; he simply clung to the Name alone. Therefore God sent him into his own abode, Vaikunth.)

The exposition of form and formlessness that the true guru Gopaldas had once given to Jivanji Maharaj — in that same manner, briefly, Jivanji Maharaj here explained it to Devidas and others: that God is beyond both form and formlessness. This sentiment has been shown. _Yadrishi bhavana yasya, siddhir bhavati tadrishi_ — (As is one's devotion, so is the fruit one attains.) Adhyaruji says: bhakt jya jevu man dhare taha teve pind — (wherever the devotee holds whatever disposition of mind, there does God take on that corresponding form). Devotees find God in the form corresponding to the devotion with which they worship him.

In the first chapter of the Sushruti Samhita, there is a statement of Lord Shivji:

_Karanam pranavasyapi Ramanaam jagadguruh ||
Tasmad dhyeyam sada chaitad yatibhih shuddha chetasa ||4||_
(Ramanandacharya, page 360)
(Shri Ram, the teacher of the universe, is the very cause even of the Om-kar; therefore let even the ascetic, with a pure mind, ever meditate upon and remember the Name of Shri Ram.)

For us, for the purpose of worship, only a Name that serves as the identifying mark of the Supreme Being is needed, and we worship the Name — let the world identify it however it may.

That is to say, having demonstrated the primacy of the Name, Jivanji Maharaj bestowed the mala and tilak upon Devdas and Ramdas; he gave mala and tilak to Haridas; he gave mala and tilak to Kalyandas and Ramdas. All these Vaishnavs had met Jivanji Maharaj in Malwa; he bestowed mala and tilak upon all of them.

In Jivandasji's Parchari (hagiographic account), Shyamdasji has given the list of Malwa's devotees as follows:

Gopaldas — Malibai
Gopaldas — Panabai
Santdas — Kaibai
Surajji Bhagat — Sahajibai
Haridas — Jivibahen
Ramdas — Panabai
Kalyandas — Baiyabai
Devdas — Jivibai
Ramdas — Jaytibai

Thus a list of these nine sant-devotees of Malwa has been given. The names of the women listed against the devotees' names are the names of their wives, who were themselves also devoted disciples of Jivanji Maharaj. All these devotees left Malwa and set out into the presence of Jivanji Maharaj, and settled permanently in Shahpura and, later, in the villages around Kanam. In our present-day community, the ancestors of many people trace back to the devotee families listed above.

Besides these, other devotees in Malwa too had accepted Jivanji Maharaj's message and word, but they were not able to leave their native land. Even today such devotees live in Malwa. We possess living evidence that in a village called Doshi there, the tradition of Namdev-Kabir is still continuing. But as a great deal of time passed and contact was broken, they became somewhat estranged from our customs and from this tradition of Jivanji Maharaj. At present many devotees come regularly from Malwa to Puniyad. Even so, much similarity is found between them and us.

In Samvat 2019, the revered Yadunath Maharaj conducted a count of the devotees' households; in it, in Surat district, in a village named Hanuman Falyu of Chanderiya, there was the house of one devotee — so it can be said that these devotees may perhaps have come from Chanderiya. Since Gopaldas was a native of Chanderiya, it may be surmised that other devotees of that village too may have come to settle in this village.

In the final stage of this journey, Jivanji Maharaj bids his last farewell to Malwa and sets forth onward toward the land of Gujarat. In this onward journey, as mentioned above, the company of saints now also accompanies him. Chanting Hari-kirtan (devotional hymns) along the way, this band of devotees moves onward toward Gujarat.
